comparisons.peer_topic: Income Tax Provision and Effective Rate
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD recorded an income tax provision of $381 million in 2024 with a 19% effective tax rate, compared to a $346 million benefit and (68%) rate in 2023. The 2024 provision increase was driven by higher pre-tax income and a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose their effective tax rates and the drivers of the income tax provision for fiscal 2024. AVGO highlights the specific quantitative impact of tax incentives ($2,261 million decrease in provision) and the associated legal uncertainty regarding the validity of those incentives. AMD reports its overall provision ($381 million) and effective tax rate (19%), attributing the change from 2023 primarily to higher pre-tax income and a specific intercompany transaction, without quantifying tax incentives in the same manner or highlighting legal uncertainty around incentive assumptions.

sentences.text: Before taking into consideration the effects of the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and other indirect tax impacts, the effect of these tax incentives and tax holiday decreased the provision for income taxes by approximately $2,261 million and $2,104 million for fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.

Our interpretations and conclusions regarding the tax incentives are not binding on any taxing authority, and if our assumptions about tax and other laws are incorrect, the benefits of the tax incentives may be adversely affected.
We recorded an income tax provision of $381 million in 2024 and an income tax benefit of $346 million in 2023, representing effective tax rates of 19% and (68%), respectively.
The increase in income tax provision in 2024 was primarily due to higher pre-tax income and a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction.

comparisons.peer_topic: Factors impacting effective tax rate and variability
comparisons.peer_summary: Changes in the volume and mix of profits, business operating models, tax audits, deferred tax valuations, non-deductible expenses, tax credits, tax holidays, tax laws (including OECD Pillar Two), accounting standards, and repatriation decisions can impact the effective tax rate and cash payments. These factors may cause significant variability in financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose risks related to the variability and uncertainty of tax incentives and holidays. AVGO explicitly warns that its interpretations of tax incentives are not binding on taxing authorities and that incorrect assumptions could adversely affect benefits. INTC lists 'expirations or changes in our ability to secure new tax holidays and incentives' alongside other factors as drivers of significant variability in the effective tax rate and cash payments. While AVGO focuses on the risk of existing incentives being challenged, INTC focuses on the variability caused by expirations and changes in securing new ones.

However, the impact on financial results differs materially: AVGO reports a significant $2,261 million benefit from these incentives in 2024, whereas MU states that due to low profitability and income mix, the benefit from tax incentive arrangements was not material in 2024 or 2023. MU notes the incentives reduced the tax provision by $1.12 billion in 2022, but AVGO does not disclose a 2022 figure in the selected text, only the 2024 and 2023 figures.
